verdict_a_product_outcome.finding: The picker membership query filters archived organizations and the resolver asks for an explicit device choice even with one open membership. However, a previously stored organization bypasses that filtered lookup in getActiveOrganizationId().
evidence: src/lib/org/active-org.ts:holdForActiveOrganizationId accepts that fast-path id and proceeds
verdict_a_product_outcome.limit: No test, build, browser, or live database verification was performed in this review.

findings.title: Archived stored organization still authorizes normal requests
findings.detail: The new archive filter only protects listMemberOrganizations callers. Request paths that call getActiveOrganizationId() return a stored id without membership/archive verification, and holdForActiveOrganizationId() then uses it. An archived selected organization can therefore continue to be sent on API calls and writes unless a UI independently runs resolveActiveOrganization first. This fails the defect's stated requirement to clear a closed prior choice and require a new explicit choice.

findings.title: First held request repeats organization enumeration
findings.detail: With no stored choice, getActiveOrganizationId() calls resolveActiveOrganization(), which lists memberships; holdForActiveOrganizationId() then calls listMemberOrganizations() again to distinguish no memberships from a pending choice. The new explicit-choice path makes this happen even for a sole open membership. This adds duplicate authenticated RPC/table reads to the first held request, though it does not affect guest behavior.

verdict_b_quality_and_doctrine.guest_auth_assessment: The shared React hook returns before organization reads when signed out. Authenticated picker reads use the existing canonical membership RPC. No guest RPC regression is apparent from source.

verification: Source-only review as requested; no product edits, tests, build, or browser actions.
